messages:
incident-bot: 🔴 SEV2 alert — GPU pool hotpath-a experiencing sustained queue growth and 429 throttles. Error spike started ~now. detected by p50 token-drop monitor. auto-escalation to #incidents triggered.
Maya (oncall): Jumping in. Observed 429s from both host-level and API gateway. Is this a capacity or rate-limit issue?
Rico (sre): Looking at the hotpath metrics — GPU utilization ~98%, queue depth up 18k, tokenbucket refill rate unexpectedly low for tier=standard. Autoscaler alerts show max_replicas hit.
Tess (infra): Autoscaler logs: "scale_request rejected: pool hotpath-a reached max_replicas=12". We had a config change last deploy to cap burst to control costs.
Jin (ops): Customer reports coming in from support: some interactive apps timing out. CS on it: @Lina please triage priority customers.
Lina (cs): Noted. Messaging top 3 paying customers with ETA. They'll want rollback/mitigation ASAP.
Maya (oncall): Hypothesis: tier tokenbucket misaligned with new autoscale cap -> requests starved for tokens while GPUs full -> upstream 429s despite queued requests. Can someone paste tokenbucket metrics?
Rico (sre): Tokenbucket breakdown (live): 
```
tier=standard: refill_rate=20r/s, burst=200
tier=premium: refill_rate=100r/s, burst=1000
active_requests: 18,342
allowed_rate_last_min: 12r/s
```
Looks like standard got throttled hard. Many requests were routed to hotpath-a (only pool supporting low-latency variants).
Tess (infra): Confirmed a policy push 2h ago changed tier->pool mapping to prefer hotpath-a for standard to reduce cross-region egress. That increased load and combined with max_replicas cap caused saturation.
Maya (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Bypass tokenbucket for existing queued requests on hotpath-a for 2 minutes to drain backlog. 2) Reroute new standard-tier traffic to coldpool-b while we scale. 3) Increase max_replicas on hotpath-a to allow autoscaler to add more. 4) Notify customers. Who can run the tokens bypass?
Jin (ops): I can run bypass via the emergency toggle. Command: `deploy-bot run toggle tokenbucket.hotpath-a.override --duration=2m --reason="drain backlog"`
deploy-bot: queued run for toggle tokenbucket.hotpath-a.override. Requires two approvals.
Rico (sre): I'll +1. @Tess please review and approve.
Tess (infra): Approving. Also kicking off scale cap bump: `infractl pools set-max hotpath-a --replicas 24` (this will take ~45s).
deploy-bot: action executed: tokenbucket.hotpath-a.override set for 2m.
Maya (oncall): Draining in progress. Observability: queue depth decreasing, 429 rate dropping. Keep an eye on downstream latency.
Rico (sre): After bypass kicked in, p95 latency briefly increased (processing backlog) but errors dropping. Autoscaler requested new nodes and infractl acknowledged new replica increase starting.
Lina (cs): Told customers we're mitigating and expect reduced errors in ~5m. They've asked what happened — will send a note that a misrouted policy + cap caused backlog, working on permanent fix.
Maya (oncall): Root cause (prelim): policy push changed tier->pool mapping increasing hotpath-a traffic for standard tier; combined with a recently lowered max_replicas cap this created a situation where tokenbucket refill looked like a shortage and started issuing 429s while work queued on GPUs.
Jin (ops): Longer term mitigations proposed on this thread: - add pre-deploy simulation for tier-to-pool mapping changes - automatic override when queue_depth > 10k to avoid token starvation - lower-risk rollout of pool-mapping changes (canary by region).
Tess (infra): Adding immediate config change: restore previous tier->pool mapping for standard to split 60/40 hotpath-a/coldpool-b. Pushing now.
deploy-bot: config push: tier-mapping.v2 -> roll forward to active.
Rico (sre): Confirming after config push: traffic redistributed, hotpath-a load down to 68% and queue depth falling to 2.1k. 429s near zero.
Maya (oncall): Excellent. Taking note for post-incident review. Action items to capture: 
- revert/optimize tokenbucket defaults for standard tier (Rico)
- add autoscale safety check so max_replicas changes trigger a policy review (Tess)
- alerting rule to fire when tokenbucket.refill << observed_incoming_rate (Maya)
- customer follow-ups and incident summary (Lina)
Maya (oncall): Handoff: I'm going offline in 30m for handover. @Rico please take lead for the post-mortem and follow-ups; @Tess you'll own infra changes. I'll add notes to the incident tracker.
Rico (sre): I'll own the postmortem, will collect metrics and timeline and schedule a blameless RCA.
Lina (cs): I'll send customer status updates and follow up with support tickets.
Maya (oncall): Thanks everyone. Leaving the channel in 25m. Closing active mitigations: token override expired, autoscaler scaled to 20 replicas (below bumped cap), load stable.
Jin (ops): Noted. I'll monitor for 1h and escalate if anything flares.
Rico (sre): Posting quick log snippet for the PM: `autoscaler.request -> rejected due to max_replicas; policy change at +2h; tokenbucket throttle ramp +4m`
Maya (oncall): Final: Severity reduced to SEV3, no data exfiltration, partial customer impact limited to elevated latency and transient 429s. Will follow-up in postmortem. :white_check_mark:
